intro: On a slope above the Silk Road at Doğubayazıt, in Ağrı province, stands İshak Pasha Palace, built in 1685–1784. In a single building it fuses Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian architecture. Let us discover how.
history: Work began in 1685 on the rock above the Doğubayazıt pass of the Silk Road, and it took about a century to finish. Inside a single walled island of building, the palace gathers a mosque, a tomb, a harem, public quarters, a council hall, a prison and baths. Look closely at the stonework: Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian traditions are carried together. And the palace is held to have had a central heating system.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the grand portal, then the harem, the mosque and the tomb, and finally the council hall.
facts: Did you know? The palace's gilded door leaves were removed to Russia in 1917, and today they are displayed in a museum in Moscow. The palace is also held to have had central heating and a drainage system, and no other residence in eighteenth-century Anatolia is known to have had either. On the same façade, Seljuk, Ottoman, Georgian and Armenian stonework stand side by side, a rare case in which no one style takes over.
outro: This brings our tour of İshak Pasha Palace to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for your company, and enjoy your visit.
